description: A task that comes back. Required: title. every ("hourly", "daily", "weekly", "2h", "90m", or a number of minutes; minimum 5) sets a cadence — LEAVE IT OUT for an ON-DEMAND task: no cadence, never due by itself, shown as a button above the input of every Dev-Agent slot running that agent and started by a click. Optional: at ("12:00", 24-hour) plus timezone (IANA, default Europe/Berlin) to pin it to a TIME OF DAY: then the next instance falls at that time whenever it was ticked off, instead of one interval after the tick. Without at it stays completion-anchored. Further optional: agent_id (whose list it belongs on — omit for your own), notes, priority, start_now (default true: the first task appears immediately; ignored when at is given, because "daily at 12" means the next 12:00). WHO RUNS IT: a series does NOT fire by itself while its agent is on trigger_mode "mcp_client" (the default) — it becomes due, appears on the list, and waits for a human in the app or an MCP client that explicitly runs the agent. Only an agent on "server_job" (update_agent) is triggered by the server itself. The result says which of the two applies in triggered_by, with a plaintext trigger_note when nobody runs it. There is never more than one open task per series: the next only becomes due once the current one is ticked off, so skipping a day leaves ONE task rather than twenty-four. Ticking it off through any route — this MCP, the app, an agent asked to do the triage — schedules the next one.

every.description: Cadence; omit for an on-demand task

start_now.description: Create the first task immediately (default true; ignored when at is set)

timezone.description: IANA zone for at, default Europe/Berlin

name: create_recurring_todo
